To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DNA repair protein O6-alkyguanine-DNA-alkyltransferase sensitizes E. coli to both the lethal and mutagentic effects of 1, 2-dibromo-ethane (DBEA) and 1, 1-dibromoethene (DBM).
DNA ATases enhance the lethality of DBE and that this effect correlates with mutagenesis.
the Ogt ATases and other DNA alkylases enhance the mutagenic and lethal effects of dibromoethane and dibromomethylene in E. coli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a cellular target for DBE- and DBM-induced toxicity and mutagenicity.
the identification of the molecular target of dihaloalkanes and the elucidation of the mechanism of the ATases in promoting their deleterious actions.
the potential of DNA repair proteins to promote the mutagenic actions induced by carcinogenic compounds and the implications of such a phenomenon for the interpretation of mutagenicity data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the O6-ATases from bacteria and mammals are able to sensitize bacteria to the lethal and/or mutagenic effects caused by DBE and, in most cases, DBM, and that this property is shared with other ATases.
the DNA alkyltransferable lesions produced by DBE and, in particular, DBM in the absence of an Ogt ATase are not lethal or mutagenic in E. coli.

the sensitization effect of ATases on DBE and DBE is not restricted to Ogt, that the effectiveness of the ATase in enhancing the deleterious effects of DBE is not related to the ability to suppress the mutagenic and lethal effects of N-nitro-somethylurea, and that the effectiveness of ATases in enhancing the deleteri-ous effects of DBE seems to be restricted to DNA alklyltransferase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DNA ATases sensitize the cells to the lethal and genotoxic actions of dibromoethane and dibromomethyl derivatives by enhancing the formation of potentially lethal lesions.

, in contrast to the protective role played by DNA alkyltransferas in preventing the lethal and mutatgenic actions of N-nitroo compounds, the DNA ATases sensitize E. coil to the lethal and genotoxic actions of DBE, DBM, and 1,2,3-trichloropropane.
the DNA alkyltransfer-ase-catalyzed removal of O6-methyl- and O6-ethylguanine lesions from DNA sensitizes bacteria to the lethal and/or mutagenic effects caused by DBE and/or DBM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mutagenicity and lethality of DBE and the mutagenicity of DBM are not prevented but rather enhanced by the DNA alkyltransfer-ase.
DNA alkyltransferasessensitize bacteria to both lethality by and mutagenesis induced by dihaloethanes, suggesting that the mutagenesis is not simply a byproduct of the lethal process.
DNA alkyltransfer-ases can promote the mutagenic and lethal activities of dibromoalkane carcinogens, and this is a property shared among bacterial and mammalian versions of the protein.
